faqs.a: iOS uses shadowColor, shadowOffset ({width, height}), shadowOpacity (0-1), and shadowRadius. Android ignores all of those and uses only elevation (a number). This generator outputs both.
faqs.q: Why do iOS and Android shadows need different code?

faqs.a: Yes, but elevation is a rough approximation. It produces a Material-style shadow based on the view's z-depth, not your color or blur. For pixel control on Android, use a custom shadow library or an SVG.
faqs.q: Does elevation match the iOS shadow exactly?

faqs.a: The most common mistake: the shadow is clipped because the parent has overflow: 'hidden', or the backgroundColor is on the wrong view. Also, on iOS, shadows need a backgroundColor on the shadowed view.
faqs.q: Why is my shadow not showing?

faqs.a: Use small offsets (0-4), moderate blur (4-10), and low opacity (0.1-0.3). Harsh dark shadows look cheap. Subtle shadows read as premium.
faqs.q: What makes a shadow look good?

faqs.a: The web preview uses CSS box-shadow, which is close but not identical to native rendering. It is a guide. Always check the final look on a real device or simulator.
faqs.q: Is the preview pixel-identical to native?

faqs.a: Often, yes. Libraries like react-native-shadow-2 give you blur and color control on Android, which elevation cannot. But for most cards and buttons, elevation plus the iOS props is enough.
faqs.q: Do I need a shadow library for Android?

react-native-shadow-generator.formula:
No math - this is a code generator. How the pieces map:

iOS (UIView shadow):
shadowColor: '#000000'        <- your picked color
shadowOffset: { width: 0, height: 4 }  <- offset X / Y
shadowOpacity: 0.25          <- opacity / 100
shadowRadius: 6              <- blur radius

Android (Material elevation):
elevation: 4                 <- separate slider, 0-24

Web preview equivalent: box-shadow: 0px 4px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25).
howTo: Pick a shadow color and adjust offset X/Y, blur radius, and opacity.
Copy the StyleSheet code or download it as a .js file, then paste it into your component.
keyFacts: React Native shadows differ by platform: iOS uses shadow* props, Android uses elevation.
iOS: shadowColor, shadowOffset {width, height}, shadowOpacity (0 to 1), shadowRadius.
Android: elevation (0 to 24+). Color and blur are not supported natively.
shadowOpacity expects 0-1, not 0-100. A common bug is passing 25 instead of 0.25.
On iOS, the shadowed view needs a backgroundColor or the shadow may not render.
Parent views with overflow: 'hidden' clip shadows. Watch out in lists and cards.
Elevation also affects draw order on Android: higher elevation draws on top.
The web preview is CSS box-shadow: close, but not pixel-identical to native.
